The weighted inverse‑error schemes (A & B) rely on highly variable weight estimates from only three validation windows and risk over‑fitting to noise.

decision.top3_series_pattern: trend_dominated, high predictability, moderate seasonality, non‑stationary, few dominant frequencies
decision.top3_why: The trimmed‑mean strategy (20 % trimming over the 5 most consistently ranked models) delivers the lowest validation score and shows the most stable per‑window performance. It is robust to the unstable model ranking and to correlated errors, which are known risks for this series. The weighted inverse‑error schemes (A & B) rely on highly variable weight estimates from only three validation windows and risk over‑fitting to noise.
decision.top3_why_not: A and B use inverse‑error weighting on a small pool; with only three windows the weight estimates have high variance and can amplify model noise, especially given the unstable ranking and correlated errors. Their per‑window scores are slightly higher and less consistent than the trimmed‑mean approach, making them less reliable for the blind test.
